wafProbeResult: all 8 batches 200 OK; no WAF markers (no cf-ray, no x-sucuri, no incapsula). HIGH confidence hasWaf=false.

watermark.reason: Celerant path-style sort (Mistake 36): the catalogUrl already contains /orderby/new-arrivals/. The probe's sort-detect tested query-form (?ordering=...) against a URL whose path already pins orderby, so both candidates returned identical first products (predictable noop). Sort IS working — it's baked into the catalogUrl path — but date monotonicity was not verified. Method C is the safe choice; a future audit can promote to Method B (navigate-from-watermark) after manually verifying that /orderby/new-arrivals/ produces a strictly date-decreasing first page.

wafWorkaround.note: Celerant emits malformed RFC-violating headers (space before colon, e.g. 'X-Frame-Options : SAMEORIGIN'). Production http-client.ts:344-347 cascades axios → native fetch on parse error. Probe path (probe/shared/fetch.ts) extended in this audit to axios → undici → curl-subprocess because the current undici release also rejects these headers. Reference: Mistake 36 in .claude/catalog-url-discovery-playbook.md.

auditNotes.fetchPathPatch: This audit added a curl-subprocess third tier to probe/shared/fetch.ts after both axios and undici rejected the malformed Celerant headers. Patch is generic — fires only on Parse Error / Invalid header token after both prior tiers fail.
